A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Rare-to-Frequent research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–P are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original R2F and R2F+ experiments on RareBench, DVMP, and T2I-CompBench, including human evaluations, ablations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, human evaluations, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Both retain the same LLM concept mapping, adaptive alternating guidance, R2F+ region-control procedure, and four-step FLUX adaptation in Appendix K. No algorithmic component changes.

E1.justification: RareBench, DVMP, and T2I-CompBench coverage is unchanged, including their single-object and multi-object scenarios. The LAION-based analyses and ImageNet-class diagnostic also remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark, backbone, guidance, and paraphrasing comparisons. Newly cited GenArtist is discussed as related work, not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Both retain the same dataset sizes, default 50 sampling steps, four-step FLUX experiment, evaluation metrics, scoring rubrics, and ten human evaluators. No experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: The guidance and stopping-point ablations, backbone/LLM comparisons, paraphrasing analysis, and appendix studies remain unchanged. These include evaluation-metric failures, R2F+ failure cases, and LAION-assisted concept mapping.

E5.justification: Both specify default seed 42, show eight-seed qualitative examples in Appendix G, and report the same uncertainty notation in Table 17. No repetition counts or statistical reporting practices change.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative examples are retained throughout. For example, Table 2 still reports R2F property scores of 89.4 for GPT evaluation and 86.3 for human evaluation; appendix Tables 15–18 also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The Gaussian assumptions, Theorem 3.1, mathematical definitions, and Appendix A proof are unchanged. Adding a Liang et al. citation to the Gaussian setup does not revise its mathematical substance.

C1.justification: Both claim training-free improvement of rare-concept composition, compatibility across backbones and LLMs, the R2F+ extension, and RareBench. The headline improvement of up to 28.1 percentage points is retained.

C2.justification: Interpretations and applicability limits remain unchanged, including explanations of frequent-concept guidance, automatic-evaluation failures, and R2F+ failures with overlapping or small bounding boxes. Appendix application discussions are also retained.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, LLM instructions, pseudocode, hardware, and resource measurements are unchanged. The abstract replaces the displayed repository URL with 'link', but its hyperlink points to the same repository.

R1.justification: v3 adds Parashar et al. on neglected tails, Liang et al. on diffusion factorization/composition, and Wang et al.'s GenArtist. These locally extend the motivation, theoretical context, and related-work citations without redefining the research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited wording edits, removes author email addresses, and changes the header from under review to publication at ICLR 2025. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Spacing, diagram sizing, and page flow are adjusted. Table 4 and Figure 7 move from page 9 to page 8, while their content is retained; no substantive figure or table redesign occurs.

improvement.justification: The added citations modestly improve attribution and scholarly context, especially around the Gaussian motivation and LLM-based image editing. The methods, empirical evidence, proofs, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
